          UEFA Women’s Champions League: Opta Supercomputer Matchday 2 Predictions
        
      
                          
                      Sep 30, 2026
          
                      Emily Clogg / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
With the help of the Opta supercomputer, we provide our UEFA Women’s Champions League match predictions across Matchday 2 in 2026-27.

It was goals galore for Lyon and Barcelona on Matchday 1 against Servette and Paris FC, respectively, whilst over in London, both Arsenal and Chelsea squeezed past their opponents with narrow 1-0 victories.
Meanwhile, reigning WSL champions Manchester City, came from 2-0 down to draw 2-2 against Bayern Munich City becoming the first English side to avoid defeat at Bayern Munich in the UWCL.
The next round of fixtures promises even more entertainment.

The blockbuster match of the week sees Chelsea travel to eight-time winners Lyon; Sonia Bompastor is set to make a return to her old stomping ground hoping to take all three points back to the English capital.
Matches elsewhere include Benfica hosting Bayern Munich, Arsenal travelling to Paris FC, and Roma facing the tough test of welcoming a formidable Barcelona to Stadio Tre Fontane.
Opta Analyst presents data-driven predictions for each game from MD2, powered by the Opta supercomputer’s pre-match simulations.
There are three 5:45pm kick-offs to start the matchday on Wednesday as BK Häcken, Paris FC and Roma host the first set of matches.
For inaugural 2025-26 UEFA Women’s Europa Cup winners Häcken, the supercomputer backs them to get the Italian job done this week after a tight 1-0 defeat at the hands of Inter Milan last time out.

This week’s opponents are six-time Serie A champions Juventus. The Bianconere won their opening league match of the season 2-0 against Napoli at the weekend, but tasted defeat in the UWCL at the hands of Portuguese outfit Benfica.
Häcken have lost each of their last three UWCL matches, equalling their longest-ever losing streak in the competition, previously set between 17 November 2021 and 15 December 2021.

The supercomputer predicts a similar fate for Juve this time around; Häcken came out victorious in 64.5% of pre-match simulations. In fact, the simulations saw more draws (19.0%) than wins for Juventus (16.5%).

Elsewhere, two-time UWCL winners Arsenal travel to the French capital to play Paris FC as they look to improve on their 1-0 win against HB Køge. The Gunners netted a stoppage-time penalty to sugarcoat what was otherwise a limp performance against the Danish side.
The big headscratcher for Renée Slegers is quite simply how to get the ball in the back of the net.

A disappointing 1-0 defeat against rivals Chelsea at the weekend leaves Arsenal seventh in the WSL table, having failed to score in two of their four games. In fact, only newly-promoted Charlton Athletic (3) have failed to score more often in league this season.

It will be the first meeting between Paris FC and Arsenal in the UWCL, with the French side having lost each of their previous three matches against English opponents in the competition, all against Chelsea (1-4, 0-4 and 0-4 between 2023 and 2025).

The Gunners came out victorious 1-0 in a pre-season friendly against their opponents this summer, and the supercomputer backs Slegers' side to start the UWCL campaign with back-to-back wins for the first time since 2022-23, coming out on top in 63.5% of the computer's 10,000 pre-match simulations.
The third and final early kick-off Wednesday has to offer comes in the form of Roma against competition giants, and favourites Barcelona.

Barça, perhaps unsurprisingly, are flying high once again this season boasting a perfect record in Liga F after five games, having scored 21 times and conceded just twice. Their quest for a fifth UWCL crown got off to a great start too as Barça dominated Servette in an 8-0 win last week.
Before the start of this year’s edition, the Opta supercomputer heavily favoured Barcelona ending the tournament as winners once again; the Blaugrana won the trophy in 41.2% of simulations.
